item_name.observed_facts: Downloadable and licensed factual footage sources
item_name.frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Compare Wikimedia Commons, Korean public works carrying KOGL marks, and Pexels as different discovery and rights systems, not interchangeable download providers.
item_name.limitations: Documentation research only; no media files were retrieved, no API keys or accounts were used, and no purchase, generation or upload was performed.

sources.frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Preserve source URL, source title, observation time, stated version/date and evidence role. Prefer the 2026 Wikimedia-specific rate policy over generic MediaWiki etiquette and current KOGL Korean type definitions over its legacy English summary.
sources.limitations: Search-result summaries were discovery aids only. The claims below rely on retrieved official pages. Null dates mean not stated or not established, not a guessed publication date. An October 2026 Pexels revision date is verified, but a clause-by-clause revision history is not.

observed_facts: Commons imageinfo returns file information and upload history. A file title/page identity, uploaded-version timestamp and SHA-1 can distinguish a repository item from a particular binary version; the uploader is not necessarily the original creator.

Pexels distinguishes a Video id, its public url, contributor user object, and multiple video_files ids/renditions. Its collections group photos and videos; the API reads featured or the authenticated user's collections but cannot create or modify collections.

KOGL is a public-work license-marking framework with content discovery, including original works available for direct download and linked works that lead to the institution's site. It is not documented here as one uniform footage-delivery API.
These sources do not document FrameForge project, sequence, production, output or saved cross-panel selections. Those semantics are not applicable provider features.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Keep provider asset identity separate from rendition identity, local file identity, sequence clip instances and production output identity. Link a selected search result to the same source record used by the bin, timeline and rights inspector.

[INFERENCE] An asset may be shared across productions, but each intended use needs its own rights/factual-use decision. Do not copy an approved status into a new commercial, political, derivative or redistribution use automatically.
project_context.limitations: [uncertain] No universal KOGL item identifier/version API or guaranteed provider-side persistent rendition history was established. Provider ids and public URLs alone cannot prove a local file is unchanged.

observed_facts: Not applicable: these footage repositories, APIs and license guides do not define a production node graph, node cancellation, partial rendering retries or saved graph execution evidence.

Pexels API requests require an Authorization header containing an API key. The documented defaults are 200 requests/hour and 20,000 requests/month. Successful 2xx responses expose X-Ratelimit-Limit, X-Ratelimit-Remaining and X-Ratelimit-Reset for the monthly period; 429 responses do not include these headers. Paginated endpoints default to 15 results and allow at most 80 per page.

Wikimedia's 2026 gateway policy applies across Action and REST API sites. Published tiers are 10 requests/minute for unidentified IP-only traffic; 200/minute for unauthenticated compliant-User-Agent bots and browser users; 200/minute for authenticated new/few-edit users; 2,000/minute for established editors. Bot-flag and certain privileged/approved/cloud clients are exempt from this gateway limit but remain subject to operational limits and robot policy. The policy recommends at most three concurrent requests and honoring Retry-After.

Generic MediaWiki etiquette recommends serial requests, batching, caching and maxlag for noninteractive jobs. Its general no-hard-read-speed-limit statement is not permission to disregard the newer Wikimedia-specific gateway limits. Commons public metadata lookup is available without a Pexels-style API key, as illustrated by official CommonsMetadata query URLs.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] If an adapter is later built, separate discovery metadata, rights review and authorized acquisition outputs. Save request parameters, provider item/rendition identity, observed status and rights evidence without storing credentials in execution records.

[INFERENCE] Cache metadata within provider rules; use provider-specific rate classes and backoff rather than one global unlimited assumption. Cancellation of a local task must not imply that provider quota consumption was undone.
node_execution.limitations: [uncertain] KOGL does not provide an established common auth/quota/error schema in the retrieved official guidance; each supplying institution/API needs separate documentation. Wikimedia explicitly warns that 2026 limits are experimental and changeable. No requests were authenticated and no rate limit or cancellation behavior was tested.

observed_facts.discovery_and_file_endpoint: Use the Commons Action API at https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php. Official documentation describes action=query, prop=imageinfo and iiprop=url|timestamp|sha1|size|mime|extmetadata for known File: titles. url yields the file URL and description-page URL; use the returned original-file URL rather than inventing a CDN path. A description page also exposes the full-resolution download link. Metadata can be retrieved without fetching the media body.
observed_facts.machine_readable_rights: CommonsMetadata provides Artist, Credit, Permission, ImageDescription, DateTimeOriginal, LicenseShortName, LicenseUrl, UsageTerms, Copyrighted, Attribution, AttributionRequired and Restrictions when available. Values may contain HTML and human-formatted dates. License is explicitly a best guess; multi-licensed LicenseShortName/LicenseUrl/UsageTerms/Copyrighted values are documented as unreliable. Missing fields do not mean permission granted. extmetadata is expensive and should be requested for only a few results at a time.
observed_facts.attribution_and_derivatives: Check each file's actual license. CC BY commonly requires creator credit and license information; ShareAlike licenses can require adaptations to carry compatible terms. Public-domain material may not require copyright attribution in some jurisdictions, but provenance credit is recommended. Credit the creator rather than automatically the uploader. The Commons site-text license is not a universal media-file license.
observed_facts.commercial_and_redistribution: Commons media is generally free-licensed or public domain and can be reused under the selected file license, including its redistribution and derivative conditions; this is not a blanket clearance for every use. Other Wikimedia projects can host non-free fair-use material and must not be silently treated as Commons.
observed_facts.authenticity_and_other_rights: Commons provides no warranty of copyright status or licensing accuracy. Trademarks, personality/publicity, privacy and moral rights can independently restrict reuse, including commercial imagery of people. Source descriptions, upload identities and timestamps are evidence, not proof that the depicted event, date or place is authentic.
observed_facts.hash_and_retention: imageinfo documents SHA-1 for the uploaded file version, alongside timestamp, size and history. A source hash establishes binary identity/integrity evidence, not copyright ownership or factual truth. No provider-mandated FrameForge hash retention period was found in these references.

observed_facts.discovery_and_file_endpoint: Current KOGL navigation distinguishes original public works, described as directly downloadable, from linked works that send users to the institution's page. The freeUse guide itself links an MP4 educational file under its upload_recommend path, demonstrating a documented file link rather than a YouTube search URL; that educational asset was not downloaded or cleared as production footage. A blanket downloadable-video API or universal file URL shape is not established.
observed_facts.machine_readable_rights: The official type guide defines license marks/types, not a verified common JSON footage schema. Read the exact item-level mark and rights notice at the supplying institution. Do not map KOGL to an identical Creative Commons license merely because the conditions resemble it.
observed_facts.current_type_matrix: Type 0: no attribution condition, commercial and noncommercial use and derivatives allowed. Type 1: attribution, commercial and noncommercial use and derivatives allowed. Type 2: attribution, noncommercial only, derivatives allowed. Type 3: attribution, commercial use allowed, modifications/derivatives prohibited. Type 4: attribution, noncommercial only, modifications/derivatives prohibited. Type 0 and AI type were introduced in the dated 2026-01-28 notice; a four-types-only summary is now incomplete.
observed_facts.attribution_and_redistribution: For Types 1-4, the official attribution example identifies institution, creation year, work title, author, KOGL type and source site; hyperlink the source when possible and never imply institutional sponsorship. Type 1 explicitly allows online/offline sharing and derivative/commercial use under its terms. Violating conditions terminates permission. The Type 1 terms say conditions may change and prior users may continue the same work without changing the purpose of use; preserve dated evidence rather than assuming all future uses are grandfathered.
observed_facts.ai_boundary: The AI mark can accompany Types 1-4; it cannot accompany Type 0. Its additional allowance is for AI training data, with conditions against substantially similar outputs and requirements around direct quotations, and a prohibition on reselling the training data. For non-training uses, the accompanying ordinary KOGL type still applies. An AI mark is not permission to edit Type 3/4 footage into a commercial documentary.
observed_facts.authenticity_and_other_rights: Type 1 terms disclaim accuracy and continuous provision. They require respect for moral rights, including avoiding misleading changes to statistics or context-destroying crops. The English type guide calls for separate permission for intellectual property rights beyond the institution's copyright. Government hosting and a KOGL mark do not establish all third-party privacy/publicity permissions or factual relevance.
observed_facts.hash_and_retention: No universal KOGL file hash, immutable revision identifier, retention term or file-delivery SLA is established by the retrieved guidance. A visible item mark must be captured with the specific file/use evidence.

observed_facts.discovery_and_file_endpoint: The current reference directs video requests to https://api.pexels.com/v1/videos/. It documents GET /v1/videos/search, GET /v1/videos/popular and, unusually, GET /v1/videos/videos/:id for a single video. Preserve this documented double-videos path rather than silently normalizing it. The legacy /videos/ path is described as due for future deprecation, not conclusively already disabled. A Video contains video_files[] with rendition id, quality, file_type, width, height, fps and link. link is where that rendition is hosted; public url is the Pexels detail page and image/video_pictures are previews, not the footage. Documentation examples include both MP4 and HLS links, so choose a supported rendition rather than assuming every link is one downloadable MP4.
observed_facts.machine_readable_rights: The documented Video schema provides asset/rendition ids, creator user metadata, duration and technical file metadata, but no authoritative per-video license object, verified release object, capture location/date attestation or cryptographic hash. The current terms distinguish explicitly marked CC0 content from Pexels-License content; do not infer CC0 from the absence of a license field.
observed_facts.attribution: The base license and terms do not require credit, although they appreciate it. Separately the API guidelines require a prominent Pexels link whenever making API requests and say always to credit photographers when possible with a link to the item. Those API integration obligations remain relevant even if a finished video's base content license does not require an on-screen credit.
observed_facts.commercial_derivatives_and_redistributio: Terms updated 2026-10-20 grant qualifying non-CC0 content commercial/noncommercial download, use, copying and adaptation rights subject to prohibited uses. Selling or distributing standalone content is prohibited, including raw video files. Merely cropping, resizing, recoloring or filtering remains standalone; a new creative work can combine media, text, audio and editing. Stock-library replication, wallpaper/core-functionality copying and unauthorized bulk/systematic copying are restricted. Commercial uses of content depicting trademarks/logos/brands in relation to goods/services are restricted. Political, misleading, offensive and other prohibited contexts require particular scrutiny; free commercial use is not unconditional.
observed_facts.authenticity_and_other_rights: The current terms prohibit contributor uploads created with generative AI but expressly do not guarantee that all content is human-produced or reliable. They disclaim that model/property/other third-party consents have been obtained; the user remains responsible for determining additional permissions. A stock scene is not evidence that a named person or historical event actually appeared as narrated.
observed_facts.hash_and_retention: No binary hash or immutable revision history is documented in the Video resource. Terms Section 11 require stopping use and removing content, including from systems/storage and clients, if an infringement claim arises as described. Perpetual content-license language is therefore not a right to retain disputed media indefinitely. No general footage hash-retention period is documented.

observed_facts: YouTube boundary: a public search or watch URL is not an authorized file endpoint. Developer Policies III.E.1 prohibit API clients downloading, importing, backing up, caching or storing audiovisual content without YouTube's prior written approval. A visible or CC-labeled video does not turn a search URL into a supported downloader; use a separately authorized source-file delivery path and its permission evidence.

The reviewed sources support four separate questions: what source/binary was obtained; what copyright license applies; whether other rights/consents permit this intended use; and whether the footage actually supports the factual statement. None is resolved merely by a search result or file hash.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Implement an evidence manifest containing provider/id, rendition id, source/detail URL, original-source chain, creator credit, exact license/version/URL and captured terms, commercial/derivative/redistribution conditions, other-rights/release evidence, capture-date/place claims, editorial relevance, retrieval time, response status and chosen file URL. Sanitize HTML metadata before display. Unknown rights must not collapse to an approved badge.

[INFERENCE] On a separately authorized future import, retain the source SHA-1 when supplied and compute a local SHA-256 of the actual received bytes. Keep original-versus-proxy-versus-edited-output hashes and transformation lineage separate. No hash was computed here because no footage was downloaded. A recommended hash policy is a FrameForge design, not a provider requirement.

[INFERENCE] Restrict automatic commercial edited-video selection to individually verified suitable licenses, such as appropriate Commons licenses, KOGL Type 0/1 or compliant Pexels uses. Route KOGL Type 2/4 commercial use and Type 3/4 editing to a separate-permission review. Route absent/multiple conflicting rights or release data to review, not inference of permission.

[INFERENCE] Add distinct labels for documentary evidence, illustration/B-roll, reconstruction and unknown factual relevance. Store the narration claim/time range the clip is intended to support; authenticity and relevance need editorial review separate from rights clearance.

[INFERENCE] Preserve minimal lawful provenance evidence according to a reviewed retention/deletion policy, not an indiscriminate permanent raw-provider-data archive. Do not include API credentials, unrelated member profile data or unnecessary personal information. Takedown workflows must remove media while handling any legally permitted minimal audit evidence separately.
footage_provenance.limitations: [uncertain] No live asset-specific copyright clearance, release verification, factual authentication, KOGL common API/download schema, KOGL quotas, provider URL lifetime or provider-compliant long-term metadata retention permission was established. Only documented file-reference contracts were verified, not media endpoint availability or actual bytes. Pexels current terms were read, but no historical diff proves which clauses changed on 2026-10-20.

observed_facts: Not applicable as an editor comparison: the reviewed providers document discovery, metadata, license conditions and collections rather than an integrated source monitor, timeline, graph and inspector.

Pexels has API-read collections and preview pictures. Commons has file-description pages and original-file links. KOGL explicitly separates direct original-work downloads from institution-page referrals. These are different navigation targets, not proof of an editable imported media object.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Use discovery results, source bin, source monitor and rights inspector within the same production context. Keep selected asset/rendition stable while opening the source page or switching to the sequence.

[INFERENCE] Distinguish Open source page, Review rights and Import authorized file. A preview playing successfully is not evidence that the source can be imported, edited or published. Surface direct-download versus referral-only status and attribution next to the result, not after export.
editing_workspace.limitations: No live UI interaction or editor navigation was observed. These are documentation-grounded design inferences, not implemented FrameForge behavior.

observed_facts: Provider APIs and KOGL licenses do not define video-channel templates, live-linked production instances, channel credentials or branded sequence reuse. These semantics are not applicable provider features.

Pexels collections are groupings, not editable production templates, and the API cannot create or modify them. Pexels prohibits raw standalone distribution and replication of core stock-service functionality. KOGL permission depends on type and purpose; Type 1 changed-condition continuation is limited to prior use without a changed purpose. Commons license terms remain attached to reused/adapted files.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] A channel template may pin a reviewed source record and attribution recipe, but each production instance must re-evaluate the new narration, commercial/political context, derivatives and redistribution destination. Do not imply that approval of one episode licenses all future contexts.

[INFERENCE] Separate reusable edit/branding parameters from provider credentials and destination-account authority. Do not package a template as a downloadable Pexels raw-footage library; source-file redistribution needs its own permission assessment.
template_channel_reuse.limitations: [uncertain] Permission for a particular FrameForge cloud cache, reusable template asset bundle or cross-customer source-file redistribution cannot be concluded from these general docs; it requires the specific distribution model and applicable provider terms/approval.

observed_facts: The providers do not document a version-specific production approval system. Rights clearance, final edit approval, local export, transfer to a destination and public publication are separate concepts; no provider document makes one imply the others.

Pexels can require removal following infringement claims; KOGL condition violations terminate permission; Commons provides no warranty of copyright accuracy. Saved prior evidence supports review but does not automatically defeat a legitimate claim.

YouTube Developer Policies require user-controlled write actions and explicit choice of public/private/unlisted visibility. This research does not establish upload method quotas or a video's actual privacyStatus, because this comparison concerns footage sources, no channel/video was accessed and no upload occurred.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Bind clearance to the original binary hash, license evidence, exact used clip segment and stated use; bind final editorial approval to the rendered artifact hash and destination/visibility. Invalidate relevant approval when the source, rendition, narration, edit, attribution or destination changes.

[INFERENCE] Block publication when required attribution, rights evidence or factual review is missing. Show the approved final version, credit text and destination before a separate explicit delivery action. Read back destination status after a future authorized upload instead of treating a source import or export as publication.

[INFERENCE] Model takedown separately from normal re-editing, including affected production instances, stored media, proxies and customer deliveries; do not silently replace disputed footage while retaining an approved label.
approval_delivery.limitations: [uncertain] No actual approval, provider integration, destination permission, post-upload visibility or takedown execution was verified. YouTube upload OAuth scopes and method-specific quota contracts are outside this source-comparison result and must not be inferred from its download-policy citation.

observed_facts: Not applicable to the headless API/license contract as a UI implementation. The retrieved documentation does not establish complete keyboard interaction, focus retention, screen-reader behavior or responsive production-workspace layouts.

The KOGL pages expose skip-to-content/main-menu links and an accessibility certification badge in retrieved markup. This is evidence of those links/badge only, not a verified WCAG conformance level, current certification validity or tested usability. Pexels' documented Photo alt field is for photos; do not invent an equivalent required description field for every Video.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Provide keyboard-accessible result selection, descriptive link names, persistent focus when the rights inspector opens, text equivalents for license marks and non-color-only rights status. Keep attribution and source links reachable at narrow widths.

[INFERENCE] Make thumbnail descriptions and editorial annotations explicit content fields; do not claim provider preview metadata is an accessibility-complete transcript or audio description. Test the eventual workspace separately.
accessibility_responsiveness.limitations: [uncertain] Keyboard, assistive-technology, mobile/reflow behavior and WCAG compliance were not tested or established by the reviewed docs. No browser session was used.
